verified_key_information_units.information: AS Tallinna Vesi reported strong financial performance in 2025 with revenue increasing 11.4% to €72.48 million, operating profit rising 11.8% to €21.22 million, and net profit growing 7.2% to €14.24 million. The company invested €55.74 million in fixed assets.

candidate_sentences.text: The group’s total sales for 2025 reached 72.48 million euros, representing an increase of 11.4% or 7.40 million euros compared to 65.08 million euros in 2024.

Operating profit grew by 11.8% to 21.22 million euros compared to 18.98 million euros in 2024, supported by the optimisation of electricity costs following the full commissioning of the combined heat and power plant at the Paljassaare Wastewater Treatment Plant.

Profit before taxes increased by 18.0% to 17.43 million euros, while net profit for the reporting period rose by 7.2% to 14.24 million euros compared to 13.28 million euros in 2024, with net profit growth partially moderated by a higher income tax rate on dividend payments.

Non-current assets increased to 341.35 million euros, largely driven by significant fixed asset investments totaling 55.74 million euros in 2025, up from 49.53 million euros in 2024, focused on maintaining asset reliability, infrastructure modernization, and environmental compliance.

verified_key_information_units.information: Customer revenue mix shifted significantly due to regulatory tariff harmonization: private customer sales increased 18.3% to €31.84 million from higher consumption, while business customer sales decreased 2.7% to €16.76 million following reduced tariff rates for businesses.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales section breakdown tables and text

verified_key_information_units.information: Cost optimization and energy transition efforts reduced electricity expenses through the new combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, which supplied 43.8% of site electricity needs and increased renewable energy consumption to 87% of total energy use (from 23% in 2020).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Energy use and energy consumption overview section

candidate_sentences.text: Operating profit grew by 11.8% to 21.22 million euros compared to 18.98 million euros in 2024, supported by the optimisation of electricity costs following the full commissioning of the combined heat and power plant at the Paljassaare Wastewater Treatment Plant.

Key environmental achievements included the full operational capacity of the combined heat and power plant, which generated all heating and over half of the electricity required for wastewater treatment processes, and recognition as the Green Company of the Year.

verified_key_information_units.information: Infrastructure modernization advanced with smart water meter rollout covering over 80% of customers (targeting 100% by end-2026), construction of 45.1 km of pipes (49% via trenchless methods), and launch of trenchless sewer rehabilitation service by subsidiary Watercom renewing approximately 6 km of pipes.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Investing for the Future; Watercom activities

candidate_sentences.text: Non-current assets increased to 341.35 million euros, largely driven by significant fixed asset investments totaling 55.74 million euros in 2025, up from 49.53 million euros in 2024, focused on maintaining asset reliability, infrastructure modernization, and environmental compliance.

Business operations were significantly influenced by strategic investments in renewable energy production, smart water meter rollouts reaching over 80% of customers, and trenchless pipeline construction methods.

verified_key_information_units.information: The company achieved 99.5% compliance with drinking water quality standards and was awarded 'Green Company of the Year'. Environmental initiatives included constructing 7.1 km of separate stormwater systems to reduce flooding and setting ambitious climate targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% from 2020 levels by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Highlights from 2025; Sustainability Statement; Climate change section

candidate_sentences.text: Key environmental achievements included the full operational capacity of the combined heat and power plant, which generated all heating and over half of the electricity required for wastewater treatment processes, and recognition as the Green Company of the Year.

Overall, the company maintained high service quality standards, with 99.5% of tap water samples complying with drinking water standards and treated effluent outperforming legal requirements, successfully navigating operational challenges while advancing its long-term strategic and sustainability objectives.

verified_key_information_units.information: The group maintained a strong liquidity position with €11.29 million cash balance at year-end and €160 million outstanding loans carrying an average interest rate of 3.24%. In December 2025, €5 million was drawn under a €25 million loan agreement with the Nordic Investment Bank to support future investments.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of financial position; Investors section

candidate_sentences.text: Outstanding borrowings increased to 160.0 million euros from 118.0 million euros at the close of 2024, reflecting long-term financing drawdowns under agreements with the Nordic Investment Bank and a syndicated loan facility to support ongoing capital expenditure programs.

verified_key_information_units.information: Tallinna Vesi continued its dividend policy of distributing 50-80% of annual profit, paying €0.53 per share (80% of 2024 net profit) to shareholders in June 2025, balancing returns with investment needs.

Key 2026 strategic priorities include completing the smart meter rollout, harmonizing water tariffs for residential and commercial customers by summer 2026, advancing the ozonation project at Ülemiste water treatment plant, reconstructing secondary clarifiers at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, and executing planned investments of up to €60 million.
